wire.remote_compute.replayed.note: Printed to STDERR when a submit answered 200 rather than 201, i.e. the --idempotency-key matched an earlier submission and Radient returned THAT run instead of creating one. It must say both that no new run was created and which run this is; {run_id} is the run the server returned. Stdout is unaffected (the run id alone under --detach), and the watch or detach continues normally afterwards.

wire.remote_compute.run_identity_mismatc.role: CLI runtime message for lop exec --remote
wire.remote_compute.run_identity_mismatc.tone: plain, one sentence; commands and flags stay verbatim
wire.remote_compute.run_identity_mismatc.note: Both placeholders are run ids: {asked_for} is the id this command sent in the path, {answered} is the id in the body Radient returned. Both must be preserved and kept distinguishable, because the point of the sentence is that they differ. It reports a response this client refuses to attribute (a cached page, a proxy, or a server bug); nothing was retried or cancelled by it.

wire.remote_compute.unreadable_envelope.role: CLI runtime message for lop exec --remote
wire.remote_compute.unreadable_envelope.tone: plain, one sentence; commands and flags stay verbatim; never alarmist
wire.remote_compute.unreadable_envelope.note: No placeholders. The response body looked like Radient's envelope but carried keys outside the msg/result/error set, so this build cannot parse it: the format changed after this build was cut. It says so and names `lop-update` as the remedy; a retry cannot help.

wire.remote_compute.api_override.role: CLI warning printed to STDERR when the remote-compute API base is overridden
wire.remote_compute.api_override.tone: plain, one sentence; the variable name and the host stay verbatim
wire.remote_compute.api_override.note: {host} is the host the bearer is being sent to, WITHOUT any credential and without a path — it is the whole point of the line and must be preserved. Printed once per invocation, to stderr, so stdout stays the run id alone. It exists because the destination is otherwise invisible: a login going to a staging server must never look like one going to production.

wire.remote_compute.api_override_invalid.role: CLI refusal for an unusable LOP_REMOTE_COMPUTE_API_URL
wire.remote_compute.api_override_invalid.tone: plain, one sentence; the variable, the schemes and the literal loopback hosts stay verbatim
wire.remote_compute.api_override_invalid.note: No placeholders. The value itself is never echoed. It states the whole rule (https, or http only on 127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost, no userinfo/query/fragment) because the command exits rather than falling back to production; the last clause says that the remote-compute command did not start.

wire.remote_compute.preview_not_enabled.role: CLI error for HTTP 403 from the remote-compute API
wire.remote_compute.preview_not_enabled.tone: plain, one sentence; not a bug report
wire.remote_compute.preview_not_enabled.note: No placeholders. 403 means the server-side preview allowlist does not carry this Radient account yet, so the remedy is to wait for the preview rather than to retry or re-login. `preview` stays in parentheses as the feature's own label.
